**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Detect the 49th stage before claiming an upper refusal**

For any chain containing 49 or more valid stages, `cw-count M f 48` can only return 48, so the new `> n 48` condition is unreachable. Such chains—including the documented 49- and 96-stage qualification variants—are therefore admitted as a 48-stage fused prefix rather than refused, contradicting `source-review.json`'s `EXPLICIT_UPPER_REFUSAL` result and `candidate-source-receipt.json`'s `explicitUpperRefusal: true`; count or probe one additional stage before enforcing the bound.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reserve space before expanding to 48 stages**

When a valid compilation is close to `MM-CODE-CAP`, increasing this expansion from 16 to 48 stages can make a source that previously fit fail with `E-GEN-FULL`: `cw-entry` has no code-capacity headroom check, and every added load/narrow/store is sent directly through `gn-emit`, which records that fatal error at the boundary instead of falling back to the original body or the 16-stage form. Gate the extended form on sufficient remaining code space so this performance optimization does not regress compilability for large programs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable bytecode writes during portable replay**

On a normal writable checkout, executing this replay imports `native-gate.py`, `native_utils_local.py`, and later `source-pool.py` from the evidence directory, causing Python to create `docs/evidence/copy-chain48-20261014/__pycache__/*.pyc` outside the requested output directory. This violates the README's promise that replay writes only to the explicit scratch directory, while the added `.gitignore` merely hides the checkout mutation; disable bytecode generation or load the modules without writing caches.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
